subject: FreshWater StreamPulse onboarding: proof package request and residency details
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@freshwater.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Carmen Reyes <carmen.reyes@freshwater.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: StreamPulse as processing subprocessor for telemetry

Hi Soojin,

Quick note from FreshWater — we're onboarding StreamPulse (streampulse.ai) to handle a subset of telemetry aggregation and short-term observability logs for the FreshWater-hosted connector that integrates with Redwood. The contract addendum and the minimal dataflow diagram are attached.

Key points:
- StreamPulse will receive only anonymized telemetry and routing metadata (no customer prompt or content data).
- They will operate from EU and US regions; primary processing for our EU customers will be in Ireland.
- StreamPulse uses a managed PostgreSQL for transient envelopes and relies on our KMS (FreshWater KMS) for envelope keys; they do not hold raw keys.

Please confirm whether Redwood needs any additional artifacts beyond the addendum and SOC2 excerpt we attached — happy to provide a longer evidence bundle if required.

Thanks,
Liam
Ops, FreshWater Labs

Attachments: streampulse_subproc_addendum.pdf, dataflow_diagram_streampulse_v1.png, SOC2_Type_II_redacted.pdf
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@freshwater.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: StreamPulse as processing subprocessor for telemetry

Hi Liam — thanks for the heads up and for sending the addendum. A few clarifying asks from our side to close the compliance loop for EU customers: 

1) Residency and routing: can you confirm the specific Ireland datacenter region (e.g., eu-west-1 equivalent) that StreamPulse will target for EU customer traffic? We need this to validate residency commitments in our DPA appendix.

2) Key custody: you note they rely on FreshWater KMS — does StreamPulse ever have write access to the KMS or only encrypted envelopes are written to their DB? Any KMS audit log export we can reference would help.

3) Data scope: please confirm a precise list of fields sent to StreamPulse (sample schema or redacted CSV is fine). The addendum says "anonymized telemetry" but we need explicit confirmation there is no PII or message identifiers tied to content.

4) Controls evidence: can you share the SOC2 page referencing change control and data deletion timelines (we received a redacted SOC2 but we couldn't find the deletion SLA paragraph).

Ben / Marissa — flagging for encryption and evidence review. If we get the three items above, should be enough for a short internal approval; may still need legal to check the addendum language.

Cheers,
Soojin
Security Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Carmen Reyes <carmen.reyes@freshwater.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@freshwater.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 08:39:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: StreamPulse as processing subprocessor for telemetry

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the detailed review. Quick answers below and we've uploaded a short evidence packet to the Drive link included. I'll also send a doc with the schema export.

1) Residency: StreamPulse will process EU traffic in Dublin (eu-dublin-1).
2) KMS: StreamPulse never has KMS write permissions. Encrypted envelopes are written by StreamPulse but key wrapping/unwrapping happens through FreshWater's KMS gateway. We included an excerpt of KMS access logs for last 30 days in the Drive folder.
3) Data fields: attached a redacted CSV sample called streampulse_payload_schema.csv — it contains timestamps, anonymized routing hashes, latency_ms, and connector_version. No message ids, no prompt/text payloads.
4) Deletion SLA: per StreamPulse contract they persist ephemeral telemetry for up to 30 days by default; deletion policy excerpt is in the evidence PDF (page 6).

We're happy to sign any reasonable addendum language you require; we did include a clause on onshore fallback for EU customers if StreamPulse changes residency, but let us know if you need stronger guarantees.

Regards,
Carmen Reyes
Senior Counsel, FreshWater Labs

Attachments: (streampulse_payload_schema.csv in Drive), link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-freshwater-evidence
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: StreamPulse as processing subprocessor for telemetry

Looping in my checklist results after a quick pass on the artifacts Carmen uploaded: 

- Residency: Dublin (eu-dublin-1) documented — matches our onboarding expectations.
- KMS: Good, StreamPulse has no write access. We will request the KMS audit log slices (UTC timestamps) for cross-check; Carmen said they put 30-day excerpts in Drive.
- Data schema: payload looks fine (no text fields). I flagged two fields (routing_hash, connector_version) for product to confirm they can't be correlated back to customer identifiers — Marissa, can you confirm?
- Retention: 30 days is acceptable for telemetry. We should add a requirement for immediate purge on contractual termination (30 days max + documented purge request).

Action items I suggest: 
1) Soojin / Security: confirm purge-on-termination language we need.
2) Marissa: confirm the non-identifiability of routing_hash.
3) Legal (FreshWater): sign a one-paragraph addendum clause guaranteeing EU residency and purge-on-termination commitments.

I'll draft the short clause after Marissa confirms the hash semantics.

-Ben
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Carmen Reyes <carmen.reyes@freshwater.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: StreamPulse as processing subprocessor for telemetry

Thanks everyone — quick confirmation from product/security review:

- routing_hash: deterministic hash of connector_id + day-window; on its own it cannot be reversed to retrieve customer identifiers. We confirm no downstream joins to our customer DB are planned at StreamPulse.
- connector_version: version strings only; no PII.

Soojin: purge-on-termination clause suggestion below (short paragraph we can include in the addendum):
"Upon termination or contract expiration, StreamPulse shall permanently delete all telemetry data received from FreshWater within 30 calendar days and provide a signed attestation of deletion, including relevant deletion timestamps and identifiers for cross-reference."

Carmen: if FreshWater can confirm acceptance of that wording and record of Dublin residency (and provide the KMS audit log slice), we can mark this subprocessor as acceptable for EU-facing customers.

Marissa Cole
Product Security, Redwood Inference
